t.1.222.1: A hawk seized that little mouse as it darted out of this hole, grasping it in its two feet and carrying it off; so there will be no danger from it.
t.1.222.2: We do not know in any way that the rat was carried off by the hawk; there will be others here as well, and from them too there is only fear for us.
t.1.222.3: It is uncertain whether the fire will reach us, for the wind has been seen to turn back; but death at the hands of the creatures dwelling in the hole would be ours without doubt, mother.
t.1.222.4: A doubtful death, mother, is better than a certain one. Fly in the sky as is proper; you will find your sons fine and well.
t.1.222.5: I myself saw a hawk coming close to the hole, and the mighty bird seized the rat as it scurried about and carried it off from the hole.
t.1.222.6: As that hawk flew off, I hurried after it from behind, invoking blessings upon him who was carrying away the mouse from its hole.
t.1.222.7: O king of hawks, you who speed away carrying off our foe, rise up to heaven and be free of enemies and golden!
t.1.222.9: Enter the hole, my sons, without fear; there is no danger for you. The rat was carried off by a hawk while I watched, there is no doubt of it.
t.1.222.8: When he had been devoured by that hungry bird, I then took leave of him and returned toward home.
t.1.222.10: Mother, we do not know that the mouse was carried off from here earlier. Without knowing this for certain, we shall not be able to enter the hole.
t.1.222.11: For I know well that that mouse was carried off by a hawk; therefore there is no danger. Let my word be done.
t.1.222.12: You should not try to free us from this great fear by a false stratagem; when minds are thrown into confusion, such a thing is not done with real deliberation.
t.1.222.13: We have done you no service, nor do you know who we are; though you yourself are tormented, you sustain us. Who are you, and who are we to you?
t.1.222.14: You are young and lovely, and able to seek out a husband. Follow your own husband, and you will obtain fine sons.
t.1.222.16: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the Śārṅgī then left her sons in the Khāṇḍava and went in haste to a safe place, one beyond the reach of Agni.
t.1.222.15: Even we, having entered the fire, shall attain auspicious worlds; and if the fire should not burn us, then you may come back to us once again.
t.1.222.17: Then the blazing oblation-bearer, sharp-flamed, came to the place where those Śārṅga birds, the little sons of Mandapāla, were.
t.1.222.18: The Śārṅgas saw the fire blazing with its own splendor, and then Jaritāri made his voice heard by Pāvaka.
